text:
I


I am time between two eternities.

Before me, eternity; and after

me, eternity. The fire;

a solitary shadow amid immense brightnesses.


Fire of time, noises, tempests;

if I gather all my strength,

I feel my eyes immense, I see blind,

and hear apples, solitudes, fall.


God inhabits my death, God lives me.

Christ, who was God in time, may draw

perfect branches from my native ceiba.


I am time, last and first time,

the time that neither dies nor kills,

tempered by zenith and star.


II


No solitude like mine.

I had everything and have nothing left.

Virgin Mary, give me your gaze

so that I may set my course straight.


Nothing remains in my eyes but a day

with vegetation stabbed through.

Do not hear me weep any longer for the wept-over

solitude in which I am, Virgin Mary.


Give me to drink the substantial water

that in every swallow holds the rose’s

and star’s scent and jewel-case.


Change my words; come before

the night lights, and silently

you will place a star in my hands.

translation.title: Nocturnal Sonnets
translation.editorial_note: The two numbered sonnets and their theological, vegetal, and astral imagery are retained. The obvious OCR glyph ‘E1’ is read as ‘El.’
